questions.q: Which sentence describes a business that produces physical goods rather than providing advice?
options: The company manufactures industrial components.
The company advises clients on financial planning.
The company provides bookkeeping services.
The company offers legal consulting services.
questions.explanation: Manufactures désigne une production de biens. Advises, provides bookkeeping services et consulting décrivent ici des prestations de service.

questions.q: A firm provides accounting services but does not develop software. Which description stays faithful to those facts?
options: The firm sells only equipment used by accounting departments.
The firm provides accounting services to its clients.
The firm manufactures accounting software for sale.
The firm develops software and provides all related hardware.
questions.explanation: Le verbe et son complément doivent décrire l’activité réelle. Utiliser un logiciel pour travailler ne signifie pas que l’entreprise le fabrique ou le commercialise.

questions.q: A company profile says the business “distributes” equipment. A translation says it “manufactures” the equipment. What distinction has been lost?
options: Paying wages versus borrowing from a bank
Recognising revenue versus measuring a profit margin
Reselling or supplying goods versus producing them
Selling goods versus collecting trade receivables
questions.explanation: Distributes ne démontre pas la production des biens. Le profil doit distinguer le rôle commercial de distribution et l’activité de fabrication.

questions.q: A business has one office in France. The source gives no information about foreign operations. Which opening avoids adding unsupported scope?
options: The business serves only French customers because its reported office is in France.
The business has no foreign activity because no foreign office is mentioned.
The business’s French office is its registered headquarters, although the source does not identify its legal seat.
The business operates from an office in France.
questions.explanation: Une localisation établie peut être rapportée directement. Elle ne permet pas d’inventer une présence internationale ni un rang concurrentiel.

questions.q: A firm “outsources payroll processing” to another company. Which summary accurately describes that arrangement?
options: An external provider processes payroll for the firm.
The firm brings payroll processing back into its own internal department.
The firm relocates payroll to another office it owns, without using an external provider.
The firm purchases payroll software while continuing to process payroll entirely with its own staff.
questions.explanation: Outsources indique le recours à un prestataire externe pour la tâche. Cette relation ne prouve ni une production de logiciel ni une acquisition du prestataire.

questions.q: A supplier both designs machines and provides maintenance. Which profile preserves both activities?
options: It purchases machine designs solely for its own maintenance needs.
It designs machines and provides maintenance services.
It resells machines but provides no maintenance services.
It provides maintenance but performs no machine design.
questions.explanation: Une présentation doit conserver les deux activités annoncées : conception et maintenance. Les autres descriptions retirent une activité ou inversent le rôle de fournisseur.

questions.q: Which stakeholder purchases goods or services from the company in the transaction being described?
options: An employee
A lender
A customer
A supplier
questions.explanation: Customer désigne l’acheteur dans la relation considérée. Supplier fournit un bien ou service, employee travaille pour l’entreprise et lender lui prête des fonds.

questions.q: A bank lends funds to a business to finance equipment. Which role does the bank occupy in that financing relationship?
options: Customer of the equipment
Employee of the borrower
Supplier of the manufactured goods
Lender
questions.explanation: Le rôle décrit est celui d’un prêteur : la banque met des fonds à disposition. Elle n’est pas, pour cette opération, l’acheteur du matériel ou un salarié.

questions.q: A presentation labels the people employed by a company “suppliers” simply because they contribute to production. Which term should identify their employment role?
options: Employees
Customers
Shareholders
Lenders
questions.explanation: Le statut décrit est celui de personnes employées par l’entreprise. Contribuer à la production ne suffit pas à faire d’elles des fournisseurs indépendants.

questions.q: An investor owns shares, while a bank holds a loan receivable against the same company. Which distinction should the profile preserve?
options: The investor and bank both hold ownership shares solely because they provide finance.
The investor is a shareholder and the bank is a lender.
The bank is a shareholder, while the investor holds the loan receivable.
The investor and bank are both lenders, with no ownership interest arising from the shares.
questions.explanation: Shareholder décrit une détention de titres de capital ; lender une relation de prêt. Financer la même entreprise n’efface pas cette différence de rôle.

questions.q: Company A buys maintenance from B and sells office equipment to B. How should their roles be described?
options: A remains only a supplier, even in the maintenance transaction in which it buys from B.
B remains only a customer, even when it provides the maintenance to A.
Their customer and supplier roles depend on the transaction.
Their roles are fixed by which company first entered the commercial relationship.
questions.explanation: Une même organisation peut être cliente dans une opération et fournisseur dans une autre. Le commentaire doit préciser le sens de la relation décrite.

questions.q: A company profile says the new branch "broke even" in its first year. In this report, the phrase refers to revenue matching total expenses. What result is described?
options: A profit equal to the branch’s total revenue.
A cash balance necessarily equal to zero at year-end.
Revenue equal only to the branch’s variable expenses, regardless of fixed expenses.
Neither a profit nor a loss under that definition.
questions.explanation: Break even refers here to a zero accounting result under the given definition. It does not state the cash balance or ignore fixed expenses.

questions.q: A staffing note counts each of 20 employees once in "headcount", including 10 who work half-time. It also reports full-time equivalents. Which distinction should the profile preserve?
options: Headcount counts people; full-time equivalents adjust the stated working time to a full-time basis.
Headcount and full-time equivalents both necessarily equal 20 because each employee is counted once.
Headcount counts only full-time employees, while full-time equivalents count all people without adjustment.
Headcount adjusts for hours, while full-time equivalents ignore whether employees work part-time.
questions.explanation: The note defines headcount as people counted once. On the stated schedules, full-time equivalents would be 10 + 10 × 0.5 = 15, while headcount is 20.

questions.q: A source reports a profit margin rather than a total profit amount. Which summary respects the type of measure?
options: It reports the total profit amount in currency units without a denominator.
It reports profitability as a ratio under the stated definition.
It reports cash receipts as a proportion of outstanding customer invoices, without regard to the stated margin definition.
It reports the increase in sales between periods rather than the profit ratio defined by the source.
questions.explanation: Une marge exprime un rapport défini, et non directement une quantité vendue, un total d’actifs ou une somme d’encaissements. Le périmètre du ratio doit rester explicite.

questions.q: A report defines "organic growth" as growth excluding acquisitions and disposals. Total revenue includes a newly acquired subsidiary. What should a profile avoid?
options: Distinguishing organic growth from the total reported revenue change.
Identifying which acquisition effects the organic-growth measure excludes.
Describing the total revenue increase as organic growth without applying the stated exclusions.
Keeping the report’s definition when labelling the organic-growth figure.
questions.explanation: The stated measure excludes changes of scope. Total growth can include the subsidiary, so its label cannot be changed to organic growth without the required adjustment.

questions.q: A report defines gross profit as revenue minus cost of sales, and operating profit after additional operating expenses. Which item can explain why operating profit is lower than gross profit?
options: A second deduction of all revenue after calculating gross profit.
The customer receipts collected after the reporting date, treated as an operating expense.
The share capital issued by the company, treated as part of cost of sales.
Additional operating expenses deducted after the gross-profit subtotal.
questions.explanation: The two subtotals differ by the additional operating expenses specified in the definition. Neither cash collection timing nor share issuance is that deduction.

questions.q: A profile calls a division "loss-making" but gives no market-share figures. Which statement preserves the meaning of that description?
options: The division reports a loss; the wording alone does not establish a loss of market share.
The division necessarily sold fewer units than every competitor.
The division necessarily lost market share despite making a positive profit.
The division necessarily had no revenue during the period.
questions.explanation: Loss-making describes a negative result, not directly a change in market share, relative sales volume or absence of sales.

questions.q: The figures suggest stronger demand, but the source gives only one month of sales. Which conclusion is proportionate?
options: The single month establishes the same growth rate for the full year without further observations.
The month may indicate stronger demand, but a longer series is needed.
The monthly rise rules out seasonal variation without a comparable seasonal series.
The monthly figure establishes a permanent demand increase without distinguishing temporary orders.
questions.explanation: Un mois peut soutenir une interprétation prudente, pas une certitude durable ou une conclusion sur tous les concurrents. La limite temporelle doit être conservée.

questions.q: A company description calls a service “the cheapest in the market” without any competitor price comparison. What evidence is missing?
options: The company’s own previous price, without prices for the competing services covered by the claim.
A comparison of customer satisfaction that does not compare prices.
A relevant comparison supporting the market-wide price claim
The lowest price among the company’s own packages, without checking the rest of the relevant market.
questions.explanation: Un superlatif concurrentiel demande une comparaison pertinente du marché. Décrire sa propre offre ou avoir un client ne démontre pas un classement de prix.

questions.q: A cost-reduction initiative is documented, but no service-quality measure is available. Which summary avoids overclaiming?
options: The saving establishes improved service quality without a separate quality measure.
The initiative’s stated intention to protect service quality counts as an observed quality result.
Customer satisfaction can be inferred from the cost reduction alone without customer or service evidence.
Costs decreased; the effect on service quality is not established.
questions.explanation: Le résultat sur les coûts est établi, celui sur la qualité ne l’est pas. Une bonne synthèse sépare ces deux dimensions au lieu de déduire l’une de l’autre.

questions.q: Company A owns all the shares in B. A profile describes B as a "wholly owned subsidiary". Which ownership statement does this expression convey?
options: A holds the entire ownership interest described in B.
A holds a minority interest in B while unrelated shareholders hold the majority.
B merely buys services from A without any ownership relationship.
A lends to B but holds none of its shares.
questions.explanation: Wholly owned describes complete ownership in the relationship given. A minority stake, service contract and loan alone do not express that ownership.

questions.q: A profile says “the figures suggest a need to review capacity”. A rewrite says “the figures prove that expansion will succeed”. What changed?
options: An interpretation about capacity became a report that expansion had already succeeded in the past.
A qualified interpretation became a guarantee of a future outcome.
A guaranteed expansion outcome became only a proposal to investigate capacity.
The rewrite preserves exactly the original strength of evidence and the same proposed action.
questions.explanation: Suggest marque une interprétation prudente ; prove et will succeed renforcent à tort la certitude et ajoutent une promesse de succès futur.
